node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Limit from left right agreement
node.description: Determine that a two-sided limit exists only when left-hand and right-hand limits agree.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Removable discontinuity as a hole
node.description: Recognise removable discontinuities where a graph has a hole but nearby values approach a common limit.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Jump discontinuity and one-sided limits
node.description: Recognise jump discontinuities where left-hand and right-hand limits are finite but unequal.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Infinite discontinuity and vertical asymptote
node.description: Recognise infinite discontinuities where function values grow without bound near a vertical asymptote.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Continuity three conditions
node.description: Check continuity at a point using existence of function value, existence of limit and equality of value and limit.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Difference quotient
node.description: Set up and simplify the difference quotient that compares function values over a small input change.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivative from first principles
node.description: Use the limit of the difference quotient to find or interpret a derivative in simple cases.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Secant to tangent limit
node.description: Connect average rates over shrinking intervals to the tangent gradient at a point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Differentiability implies continuity
node.description: Understand that differentiability at a point implies continuity there, while continuity alone does not guarantee differentiability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivative sign and increasing decreasing
node.description: Use the sign of the derivative to identify intervals where a function is increasing or decreasing.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Stationary points from derivative zero
node.description: Find stationary points by solving where the derivative equals zero and interpreting the corresponding function values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Local maximum minimum first derivative test
node.description: Classify local maxima and minima by checking changes in derivative sign around stationary points.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Second derivative concavity introduction
node.description: Use the second derivative to describe concavity and identify simple changes in curvature.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Optimisation context constraints
node.description: Set up optimisation problems with relevant domain constraints from a real or mathematical context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Related rates introduction
node.description: Use derivatives to relate rates of change between connected quantities in simple contexts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Left and right rectangle approximations
node.description: Approximate area or accumulation using left-endpoint and right-endpoint rectangle sums.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Trapezoidal rule introduction
node.description: Approximate a definite integral using trapezoids over equal or specified subintervals.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Net area versus total area
node.description: Distinguish signed net area from total geometric area when a graph lies above and below the axis.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Definite integral reversal of bounds
node.description: Interpret how reversing the bounds of a definite integral changes the sign of the accumulated value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Integral units in accumulation
node.description: Interpret the units of a definite integral as the product of output units and input units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Two sided limit needs matching sides
node.description: A two-sided limit exists only when the left-hand and right-hand limits approach the same value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivative limits a difference quotient
node.description: The derivative at a point can be defined as the limit of a difference quotient as the input change approaches zero.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Positive derivative indicates increasing
node.description: Where a differentiable function has a positive derivative, the function is increasing locally.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reversing integral bounds changes sign
node.description: Swapping the upper and lower bounds of a definite integral changes the sign of the integral.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Integral units multiply units
node.description: The units of a definite integral combine the units of the integrand with the units of the input variable.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Limit equals function value always
node.description: Learner assumes the limit at a point must equal the function value even when a hole or discontinuity is present.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Two sided limit from one side
node.description: Learner decides a two-sided limit from only left-hand or only right-hand behaviour.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivative treated as average rate
node.description: Learner treats the derivative at a point as an average rate over a visible interval rather than an instantaneous limiting rate.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Stationary point always extreme
node.description: Learner assumes every point where the derivative is zero must be a local maximum or minimum.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Integral units same as function units
node.description: Learner gives the units of an accumulated integral as only the integrand's units instead of combined units.

edge.rationale: Determining whether one-sided limits agree is central to using one-sided limits.
Removable holes are a core introductory discontinuity type.
Using derivative sign directly practises interpretation of derivatives in differentiation.
The trapezoidal rule is a core numerical integration method.
Distinguishing signed net area from total area is central to interpreting signed area.
Agreement of one-sided limits depends on understanding left-hand and right-hand limits.
edge.failure_signal: Learner decides a two-sided limit from only one side.

edge.rationale: Recognising a removable hole depends on reading nearby limiting behaviour from a graph.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats the hole's missing value as preventing any limit from existing.

edge.rationale: Jump discontinuities are identified when one-sided limits do not agree.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reports a two-sided limit despite unequal side behaviour.

edge.rationale: Infinite discontinuities require reading unbounded behaviour near an input value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reports a finite limit where values grow without bound.

edge.rationale: Checking continuity uses the function value and the limit at the point.
edge.failure_signal: Learner checks only the function value or only the graph appearance.

edge.rationale: The difference quotient formalises average rate of change over a small interval.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect quotient notation to change in output over change in input.

edge.rationale: First-principles differentiation takes a limit of the difference quotient.
edge.failure_signal: Learner simplifies a difference quotient but does not take the limiting step.

edge.rationale: The secant-to-tangent idea depends on interpreting instantaneous rate as a limiting process.
edge.failure_signal: Learner leaves the result as an average rate over a nonzero interval.

edge.rationale: Differentiability-continuity relationships require prior understanding of continuity at a point.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assumes every continuous function is differentiable everywhere.

edge.rationale: Using the sign of a derivative requires interpreting derivative notation as a function of input.
edge.failure_signal: Learner finds derivative values but cannot connect sign to behaviour of the original function.

edge.rationale: Stationary points build on understanding derivative values and sign.
edge.failure_signal: Learner solves f(x)=0 instead of f'(x)=0 for stationary points.

edge.rationale: The first derivative test classifies stationary points after they are found.
edge.failure_signal: Learner labels every stationary point as an extreme point without sign testing.

edge.rationale: Second-derivative concavity extends derivative-based graph analysis.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses slope sign with concavity sign.

edge.rationale: Optimisation with constraints relies on finding and classifying candidate extrema.
edge.failure_signal: Learner differentiates but ignores endpoints or contextual domain restrictions.

edge.rationale: Related rates rely on differentiating related quantities with respect to a common variable such as time.
edge.failure_signal: Learner differentiates variables independently without relating their rates.

edge.rationale: Rectangle approximations estimate signed area or accumulation under a curve.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts rectangles without considering height signs or interval widths.

edge.rationale: The trapezoidal rule builds on approximating area over subintervals.
edge.failure_signal: Learner averages endpoints incorrectly or ignores subinterval width.

edge.rationale: Net versus total area interpretation requires signed-area understanding.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats all below-axis area as positive contribution to the integral.

edge.rationale: Bounds reversal meaning depends on definite integral notation and orientation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reverses bounds without changing the sign.

edge.rationale: Integral units are interpreted through accumulation of a rate or density over an input variable.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives only the integrand units or only the input units.
